newsitem.title: UK: London gold rollercoasters after NY market opens.
newsitem.headline: London gold rollercoasters after NY market opens.

text.p: Gold sank to fresh 12-year lows in a wave of selling on Monday afternoon but prices bounced back after speculators took profits, dealers said.
The New York market returned after the Independence Day holiday weekend to find prices sharply lower and responded with a wave of selling.
Spot gold briefly dropped to a low of $313.90 an ounce, compared to Friday's London close of $324.25/324.75.
But a modicum of support was evident around $315.00 an ounce and speculators who had bet on prices falling took profits by covering their positions, dealers said.
As a result gold fixed barely changed at $318.00 an ounce, compared to $318.75 on Monday morning and $324.45 on Friday afternoon.

"The New York market opened way below where it closed (on Thursday) so the first thing people did was get out," a London based dealer explained. "There is some support at $315 but it's hard to tell how much -- we haven't seen these levels for 12 years."
Gold has lost about 13 percent of its value for far this year under threat of selling from central banks as they reviewed the worth of holding gold reserves.
The latest price fall came after the Reserve Bank of Australia announced last Thursday that it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves.
Market sentiment was overwhelmingly bearish, however, and traders were forecasting further losses towards $300 or lower.
However, a short-term push higher was seen possible as the market was heavily oversold, some analysts and dealers said.
"The market is so short that a covering rally has to be possible but it will be very heavily sold," said analyst Andy Smith of Union Bank of Switzerland.
Most of the attention was focused on gold but the white precious metals also felt some of its pain.
Platinum was last indicated at $410.00/$414.00, off $9.00, while palladium was at $180.00/$184.00, down $10.
Silver was following gold lower and was down 11 cents at $4.43/$4.45. Critical support was seen at $4.30.

Not helping platinum and palladium, a Russian Finance Ministry official told Itar-Tass news agency that the state precious metals export agency would resume exports of platinum group metals (PGMs) this month after long delays.
